title: Vibe-Coding Startup Lovable Doubles Valuation to $13.3 Billion With $400 Million Raise
excerpt: The Stockholm-based AI coding platform has nearly tripled its revenue in eight months and now counts Nvidia and Adidas among its enterprise clients.
body:
• Stockholm-based Lovable raised $400 million in Series C funding at a $13.3 billion valuation, exactly doubling its December 2025 figure of $6.6 billion.
  • Annual recurring revenue has nearly tripled and is tracking toward $600 million by end of August, up from roughly $200 million at the time of its last raise.
  • Menlo Ventures and the EQT-managed Scaleup Europe Fund co-led the round, with Tencent, Balderton Capital, and World Innovation Lab among new backers.
  • Enterprise clients include Nvidia, Adidas, Zendesk, and Hearst, with more than 60 million projects created on the platform since its November 2024 launch.

Swedish vibe-coding startup Lovable has raised $400 million in a Series C round that values the company at $13.3 billion, the company announced on Wednesday. The deal doubles the $6.6 billion valuation Lovable achieved just eight months ago and vaults it into the ranks of Europe's most valuable private technology companies.

Menlo Ventures and the European Commission's newly created Scaleup Europe Fund — a vehicle managed by Swedish asset manager EQT — co-led the round. New investors include Balderton Capital, World Innovation Lab, Tencent, and U.S.-based Regent. Existing backers Accel, Antler, CapitalG, and HubSpot Ventures also participated.

"This funding lets us move faster on the product, infrastructure, and team needed to make Lovable the best place to build and run a business."

— Anton Osika, CEO and Co-founder, Lovable

Revenue Growth Defies Skeptics

Lovable's financials underscore why investors are piling in. The startup is on track to hit a $600 million annual revenue run rate by the end of August, according to the Wall Street Journal — nearly triple the roughly $200 million it disclosed in December 2025. The company had previously been profitable but is now investing aggressively in product development and geographic expansion, CEO Anton Osika told the Journal.

Since its launch in November 2024, more than 60 million projects have been created on the platform, and Lovable-built applications attract over 900 million visits per month, according to company data. The platform allows users to build fully functional software applications using simple natural-language prompts — a process known as "vibe coding," a term coined by AI pioneer Andrej Karpathy.

Enterprise Adoption Accelerates

What began as a tool for non-technical founders building quick MVPs has expanded into serious enterprise territory. Nvidia uses the platform to develop customized project-tracking software for its team leaders. Other corporate clients include sportswear giant Adidas, publisher Hearst, and helpdesk provider Zendesk.

Despite using Lovable itself, Zendesk doesn't view it as a competitive threat. "Lovable can't provide the level of reliability at scale" needed to manage customer requests across multiple channels, Jorge Luthe, a Zendesk senior director of product, told the Journal.

A Rapidly Expanding Market — and Competition

Lovable operates in one of the fastest-growing segments of the AI economy. Rival Replit achieved a $9 billion valuation in March, tripling its figure from six months earlier. Cursor, another vibe-coding platform aimed at developers, was acquired by SpaceX for $60 billion in July, according to TechCrunch. Factory, which builds AI agents for enterprises, raised $150 million at a $1.5 billion valuation in April.

For Menlo Ventures, the Lovable investment represents the firm's largest single bet after Anthropic. "A testament to how bullish we are on Lovable's outlook," partner Matt Murphy told the Journal.

Staying European — For Now

The Scaleup Europe Fund's involvement carries strategic significance beyond the capital itself. The fund was created specifically to keep Europe's most promising startups from decamping to the United States as they scale. If companies like Lovable end up backed predominantly by U.S. investors, "the shift towards relocating headquarters or listing in the U.S. becomes powerful," undermining Europe's technology development, said EQT partner Victor Englesson.

Lovable plans to grow its workforce by roughly 50% to about 450 employees this year, with hiring concentrated in machine learning, product, infrastructure, and security roles across its offices in Europe and the United States. The company is also expanding into Latin America and working to improve platform security and reliability.

Osika has previously said his goal is to build Lovable into a $100 billion company while keeping it based in Sweden — a bold ambition in a European tech ecosystem that has historically struggled to retain its biggest successes.
